message.content:
Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-rays demonstrate marked tracheomegaly (dilated trachea) and extensive bilateral cystic bronchiectasis with multiple air-fluid levels, which are hallmark features of Mounier-Kuhn syndrome (tracheobronchomegaly). The progression to increased cavitation and fluid levels indicates worsening disease requiring aggressive airway clearance (physiotherapy) and antibiotic therapy for superimposed infections.
